key_insight: OmniStream presents a unified streaming visual backbone that uses causal spatiotemporal processing to simultaneously perceive, reconstruct, and act on continuous visual inputs in real time.
problem_solved: It resolves the fragmentation between image semantic models, offline temporal models, and geometric reconstructors by providing a single causal, online architecture for perception, reconstruction and action in streaming environments.
method: Causal spatiotemporal attention backbone designed for continuous, low-latency input streams and online inference.
Jointly trained pathways that produce semantic perception, dense 3D/scene reconstruction, and action/policy outputs from the same streaming representation.
Compact temporal memory and physically structured representation to support consistent reconstruction and downstream control in real time.
impact: OmniStream enables developers of robots, AR/VR, and autonomous systems to use one real-time backbone for sensing, mapping and decision-making, reducing system complexity and improving online performance and robustness.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: streaming cameras → causal spatiotemporal backbone → branches for perception, reconstruction, and action.
Temporal attention map / sliding-window timeline illustrating causal processing and memory retention.
Before/after visualization: raw video frames vs reconstructed 3D scene or depth map overlays.
Bar/line chart comparing latency vs accuracy (or reconstruction fidelity) of OmniStream against specialized baselines.
paper_title: OmniStream: Mastering Perception, Reconstruction and Action in Continuous Streams
paper_authors: Yibin Yan, Jilan Xu, Shangzhe Di, Haoning Wu, Weidi Xie
